claims.explanation: U-18666A is a cationic amphiphile that inhibits oxidosqualene cyclase and, more importantly, blocks NPC1-dependent lysosomal cholesterol egress, causing lysosomal cholesterol accumulation and impaired autophagic/lysosomal membrane trafficking. Selectivity likely reflects dependence on lysosomal cholesterol homeostasis and autophagic flux, with squamous/adenocarcinoma lines carrying TP53, SF3B1, PIK3CA, PTEN, KRAS/BRAF and chromatin-modifier mutations being most vulnerable, while PTEN-mutant CNS glioma and melanoma lines are relatively protected. The transcriptional signature (FAS up, cell-cycle genes down) is consistent with lysosomal stress and growth arrest rather than a specific kinase target.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is near-universal in the most killed lines and absent in several protected lines; loss of p53-dependent lysosomal/autophagic responses increases dependence on NPC1-mediated cholesterol t
Recurrent hotspot SF3B1 mutations in killed lung, colorectal, and esophageal lines; spliceosomal stress may synergize with lysosomal cholesterol blockade
PIK3CA mutations enriched in killed colorectal, esophageal, gastric, bladder, and breast lines; PI3K-driven anabolic/cholesterol demand sensitizes to sterol pathway inhibition
PTEN-mutant CNS glioma and melanoma lines are among the least affected, suggesting PTEN loss activates compensatory cholesterol uptake/efflux
KRAS-mutant colorectal, pancreatic, and some lung lines are killed, consistent with oncogenic RAS increasing lysosomal biogenesis and cholesterol dependence
BRAF-mutant colorectal and lung lines appear in the sensitive set, though BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are protected, indicating lineage context
U-18666A phenocopies NPC1 loss; higher NPC1 expression should buffer lysosomal cholesterol egress blockade
ARID1A mutations appear in several least-affected lines (melanoma, liver, glioma), suggesting SWI/SNF loss alters lysosomal gene programs
NF1 mutations recur in killed colorectal, upper aerodigestive, bladder, and breast lines, possibly via RAS-pathway activation
EGFR is upregulated in the virtual-cell MCF7 response and EGFR-mutant/dependent lines may have increased sterol demand
FAS is upregulated in both virtual-cell responsive lines, linking death-receptor signaling to lysosomal stress-induced apoptosis
SMARCA4 mutations appear in killed neuroblastoma and SCLC lines; chromatin remodeling loss may impair cholesterol-homeostatic transcriptional responses
